L60: ## Requirements to Complete a Course
L61: 
L62:   * Complete each Challenge by attempting each of the questions
L63:   * Achieve a total average score of 70% or better across all Challenges, Milestones, and Touchstones
L64:   * Complete your Final Milestone, which contributes to your overall course score
L65: 
L66: ## How to Drop a Course
L67: 
L68: To drop a course, go to your 【17†home page】 and under 'Active Courses,' select 'Drop Course.'
L69: 
L70: If you re-enroll in the course, you will restart from the beginning.
L71: ## Where's my Touchstone Submission?
L72: 
L73: Please expect up to 7 business days to receive your graded Touchstone assignment. We want to make sure you receive the thorough feedback you deserve.
L74: 
L75: ## Milestone Retakes
L76: 
L77: You are able to retake each Milestone assessment one time. If you would like to retake a Milestone, you can select the 'Retake' button at the top of the Milestone page. Please note: The questions are different on the retake, and only your best Milestone score will be saved.
L78: ## Average Time to Complete a Course
L79: 
L80: Sophia courses are self-paced, so the amount of time it takes to complete the course is dependent on the individual. There are some courses that have one or more Touchstone assignments, and each assignment may take up to 7 business days to be graded. Please take this into consideration if you plan to take a course with Touchstones.
L81: ## Tutoring
L82: 
L83: Some Sophia courses offer subject matter support beyond what Learning Coaches can provide. The following courses include 10 hours of free tutoring from our partner, Brainfuse. You can drop into a tutoring session 24 hours a day, schedule a convenient appointment, or ask a question offline. Additional tutoring time can be purchased as needed.

L108: ## Do Courses Have Time Limits?
L109: There are no deadlines for Sophia courses. However, you will want to keep in mind the ACE renewal dates if you intend to drop a course or if a course becomes inactive. If a course is renewed by ACE during your time taking it, and the course is dropped or goes inactive for any reason, the course will need to be reset from the beginning for you to retake. This is because when a course is renewed by ACE, we often need to make changes to the course to maintain its credit recommendation from them.
L110: To avoid a course automatically becoming inactive, make sure you work on it periodically, as it will be dropped after 180 days of inactivity.
L111: 
L112: You can view the ACE course list and see the renewal dates for all of our courses here: 【18†https://www.acenet.edu/National-Guide/Pages/Organization.aspx?oid=76099b28-9016-e811-810f-5065f38bf0e1†www.acenet.edu】
L113: ## Can I Receive a Degree With Sophia?
L114: 
L115: Sophia is not a school, college, or university, therefore, we do not award degrees. That said, each of our courses come with a national credit recommendation from the American Council on Education (ACE). More information about our course-specific ACE recommendations can be found on 【18†ACE's official website†www.acenet.edu】.

L127: # What Colleges Accept Sophia Learning Courses
L128: 
L129: Posted on August 20, 2026
L130: 
L131: By Sophia Learning
L132: 
L133: Are you considering online courses for transferable credit to potentially save time and money on your degree? If so, one of the questions you may have is, “Will my college accept Sophia courses?”
L134: Though schools have different policies, Sophia Learning partners with more than 115 colleges and universities, and transcripts have been sent to more than 2,900 institutions for review. Many schools accept Sophia's college-level courses, which are recommended for credit by the American Council on Education (ACE), a major coordinating body for U.S. colleges and universities. This means Sophia's courses have been evaluated by subject matter experts and recommended for credit transfer.
L135: Fortunately, Sophia makes it easy to research your school before you enroll. With the updated 【103†Find Your School tool】, you can explore partner institutions, search your college, and learn how to verify transferability before you begin taking courses. Find out how to potentially transfer coursework, what colleges commonly accept those courses, and how to be sure they fit into your degree plan.
L136: ## What Is Sophia Learning and How Do Its Courses Work?
L137: ### Understanding Sophia Learning
L138: 
L139: Sophia Learning offers affordable, self-paced online courses designed to help students complete college-level learning on their own schedule. Whether you’re balancing work, family responsibilities, or a busy schedule, Sophia allows you to learn whenever and wherever it’s convenient.
L140: 
L141: You can choose from more than 【100†80 courses for college】 covering many of the subjects commonly found in the first two years of college, including:
L142:   * English Composition
L143:   * Mathematics
L144:   * Biology
L145:   * Chemistry
L146:   * Business
L147:   * Humanities
L148:   * Psychology
L149:   * Information Technology
L150: 
L151: When you successfully complete a course, you can request an official Sophia transcript for your preferred school to evaluate for transfer credit. Instead of awarding college credits directly, Sophia provides college-level courses that have been reviewed for credit, allowing participating schools to determine if and how they apply toward a degree.
L152: ### ACE Recommendations and Credit Transfer
L153: 
L154: Sophia courses have been evaluated by the 【104†American Council on Education (ACE) College Credit Recommendation Service†www.acenet.edu】. An 【105†ACE recommendation】 means independent faculty reviewers have determined that a course demonstrates college-level learning outcomes and recommends an equivalent number of semester credit hours. These recommendations help colleges evaluate whether coursework may be accepted for transfer.
L155: However, it’s important to understand what ACE recommendations mean – and what they don’t.
L156: 
L157: ACE recommendations:
L158: 
L159:   * Demonstrate that coursework has been reviewed for college-level learning
L160:   * Provide guidance to colleges when evaluating transfer credit
L161:   * Can support transfer eligibility
L162: 
L163: ACE recommendations do not guarantee that every college will accept every course. Each institution has its own transfer policies and makes its own decisions.
L164: ## Why Students Use Sophia Learning
L165: 
L166: Students choose Sophia for several reasons, including:
L167:   * Students can save up to 92% on their gen eds with Sophia*.
L168:   * Flexible self-paced, online learning
L169:   * The opportunity to complete general education requirements before enrolling or while pursuing a degree
L170:   * Sophia's flexible format allows learners to complete gen ed courses 77% faster than traditional semester formats**.
L171:   * Convenient options for completing prerequisite coursework
L172:   * No semester start dates, no assignment deadlines
L173:   * No additional textbook costs
L174: For many learners – both fresh graduates and returning adult learners – transferring previously completed Sophia courses can reduce both the time and cost required to earn a degree.

L184: ## Types of Colleges that Sophia Learning Courses Commonly Transfer To
L185: 
L186: Sophia courses may transfer to a wide variety of institutions across the U.S.
L187: ### Traditional Colleges and Universities
L188: 
L189: Many public and private colleges evaluate Sophia coursework for transfer credit, particularly for gen ed requirements and electives. Each institution determines how individual courses fit within its curriculum, however.
L190: ### Schools with Established Transfer Pathways
L191: 
L192: Sophia partners with more than 115 colleges and universities, giving students streamlined transfer pathways for students attending participating institutions. Partner schools publish transfer equivalencies that show how Sophia courses apply toward specific degree requirements.
L193: ### Competency-Based and Flexible Degree Programs
L194: 
L195: Many competency-based and online degree programs welcome transfer-friendly courses that helps students accelerate degree completion. These institutions often provide transfer opportunities while maintaining their own residency requirements.
L196: 
L197: ### Community Colleges
L198: 
L199: Community colleges may also evaluate Sophia courses for transfer into associate degree programs or certificate pathways, although accepted courses and credit limits vary by institution.
L200: ### Acceptance Can Vary
L201: 
L202: Even when a college accepts Sophia courses, transfer decisions may differ depending on:
L203: 
L204:   * Your degree program
L205:   * Institutional accreditation policies
L206:   * Department requirements
L207:   * Residency requirements
L208:   * Maximum transfer credit limits
L209:   * Whether the course fulfills general education, elective, or major requirements
L210: 
L211: For example, a course that transfers into one bachelor’s program may not satisfy requirements in another at the same institution.
L212: ## Factors That Affect Whether Sophia Courses Transfer
L213: 
L214: ### Course Equivalency Requirements
L215: 
L216: Colleges compare Sophia courses with their own curriculum to determine whether learning outcomes align. General education courses often have broader transfer opportunities, while major-specific courses may require closer review.
L217: ### Credit Transfer Limits
L218: 
L219: Many colleges limit the number of transfer credits that can count toward graduation. It’s important to be aware of residency requirements as well, which require completing a minimum number of credits directly through the institution awarding the degree.
L220: ### Program-Specific Restrictions
L221: 
L222: Some academic programs have additional transfer requirements, such as:
L223: 
L224:   * Nursing
L225:   * Engineering
L226:   * Education
L227:   * Allied health
L228:   * Other professional disciplines
L229: 
L230: These fields may require students to complete certain prerequisite or core courses directly through the institution, even if gen ed courses transfer successfully.
L231: ### Policy Updates and Institutional Changes
L232: 
L233: Transfer policies evolve over time. Colleges may update transfer equivalencies, revise degree requirements, or change institutional policies from year to year. It’s crucial to verify current information before enrolling in any transferable courses.
L234: 
L235: ## How to Verify Sophia Course Transferability Before Enrolling
L236: 
L237: Just a few simple steps can help you make informed decisions before beginning your coursework.
L238: ### Review the College’s Transfer Credit Policy
L239: 
L240: Start by visiting your school’s transfer credit webpage. Look for information about:
L241: 
L242:   * ACE recommendations
L243:   * Alternative credit providers
L244:   * Transfer equivalencies
L245:   * Gen ed requirements
L246: ### Use Transfer and Partnership Tools
L247: 
L248: Sophia’s updated 【103†Find Your School page】 is a quick and easy way to start your research. You can:
L249: 
L250:   * Search for your college or university
L251:   * View Sophia partner institutions
L252:   * See whether Sophia has previously sent transcripts to your school for review
L253:   * Access additional transfer resources and tools
L254: 
L255: Remember that if your school appears as a transcript recipient, you still want to confirm how your specific courses apply to your degree program.
L256: ### Contact an Admissions or Transfer Counselor
L257: 
L258: Your academic advisor can provide guidance specific to your program. Here are some questions to ask:
L259: 
L260:   * Which Sophia courses typically transfer?
L261:   * Which courses satisfy gen ed requirements?
L262:   * Are there limits on transferable credits?
L263:   * Are any required courses excluded?
L264: 
L265: Whenever possible, ask for written confirmation for future reference.
L266: ### Obtain a Preliminary Credit Evaluation
L267: 
L268: If you’re planning to enroll soon, many institutions can perform a preliminary transfer evaluation. This gives you a clear picture of:
L269: 
L270:   * Which Sophia courses are likely to transfer
L271:   * How they’ll apply toward your degree
L272:   * What coursework you’ll still need to complete after enrollment
L273: 
L274: Getting an evaluation before taking courses can help you maximize your time and tuition savings with courses that serve your goals.
L275: ## Is Sophia Learning Right for Your College Goals?
L276: 
L277: Sophia Learning can be an excellent option for students looking to complete affordable, flexible, college-level coursework that may transfer toward a degree. If you’re ready to get started, use the Find Your School page, speak to an academic advisor, and 【102†start your free trial】.
